assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned a superconducting artificial atom into a controllable, strongly coupled quantum system inside a microwave resonator, giving dispersive readout, qubit coupling and the architecture that most superconducting quantum processors now use. It is a clean regime-opening step in which fundamental light-matter physics becomes an enabling platform, and it follows naturally from the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and co-workers) and the strong-coupling experiments (Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues) share credit across theory and experiment. Girvin is also central but at most three can be named. Schoelkopf and Wallraff carry the experimental demonstration and Blais the theory proposal; a Schoelkopf, Wallraff, Girvin configuration is a defensible alternative and I have not independently verified the precise division of credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many laboratories over two decades, with a stable interpretation and wide reproducibility; timely and arguably overdue now that the platform is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Girvin or Blais should be the third laureate is unresolved.
As a close colleague of this community I may be biased toward this field and should defer to others on competing claims.
Prize rewards the discovery, and fault-tolerant computing itself remains unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's 1995 trapped-ion quantum gate proposal and the experimental realisation of high-fidelity ion-based quantum logic and simulation established a concrete route to quantum computation and programmable quantum simulation. The theory-experiment pairing is original and has had lasting influence on the whole quantum information field.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are clear theoretical originators; Blatt is a leading experimental realiser of ion-trap gates and simulation. Other experimentalists (for example Monroe and Wineland, the latter already recognised in 2012) have strong claims, so the experimental share is not uniquely settled.
assessment.maturity: Mature, reproduced in many groups, with commercial-scale platforms developing; recognition is timely. Wineland's earlier prize partly overlaps in subject matter, which may matter for the committee.
uncertainties: Which experimentalist(s) should share with Cirac and Zoller is debated.
Overlap with the 2012 prize on controlling single quantum systems.
Candidate bundles theory proposals with several distinct experimental advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and clean, tunable many-body Hamiltonians, creating quantum simulation as a laboratory tool. The regime is genuinely new and the control is exceptionally detailed, including single-site imaging.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Hubbard-model realisation, Greiner, Bloch and Hänsch demonstrated it, and Esslinger's fermionic work is also important. Four names are credited and only three may be chosen, so one major contributor must be left out, and Zoller appears in other candidates as well.
assessment.maturity: Well established and reproduced widely, with the interpretation stable; recognition is plausible now, though some may argue it follows the 2001 condensation prize closely in lineage.
uncertainties: Selection among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller is difficult and could be contested.
Practical impact is largely as a simulator rather than a solved computational advantage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics reached the quantum regime of macroscopic mechanical motion, with ground-state cooling, quantum-state control and entanglement of mechanical resonators. It is closely tied to microwave quantum optics and to the Cleland-style demonstration of phonon quantum states in superconducting circuits, which I know from my own work on phonons coupled to an artificial atom.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg led optical and cavity optomechanics, while Cleland demonstrated quantum control of a mechanical resonator using a superconducting qubit; other groups (Lehnert, Painter, Schwab) also made decisive advances. The three-person boundary is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across several platforms and now fairly mature in the quantum regime; applications are still emerging, and the timing is reasonable but less compelling than the leading entries.
uncertainties: Several equally strong contributors are not nameable within three slots.
Not all mechanical-quantum results are equally independent of one another.
Possible bias because of the close link with my own research topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's precision demonstrations, reached fractional uncertainties around 10^-18, which transformed timekeeping and enabled tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice approach and Ye drove the extreme-precision implementation; the two-person configuration is a clean fit, though Hall and Hänsch previously received recognition for the frequency comb that Ye's work relies upon.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by many national metrology laboratories, and the redefinition of the second makes recognition timely.
uncertainties: Competition with ion clocks and the thorium work could affect how the committee frames it.
Outside my main area, so I defer to colleagues on metrology priorities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light underpins quantum-enhanced measurement, from Caves's interferometer proposal to Kimble's early squeezed-state generation and the routine use of squeezing in gravitational-wave detectors. It is a clear case where a foundational quantum optics idea became essential to an instrument.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed the use of squeezed vacuum in interferometry and Kimble produced squeezed light early on; Mavalvala and Schnabel contributed to its practical deployment in gravitational-wave detectors. Other experimentalists on early squeezing (Slusher, Wu) are not in the credited list. The allocation among four names is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is now deployed in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600, giving robust confirmation; timing is reasonable though the practical contributions are engineering-flavoured.
uncertainties: Early experimental credit may be missing from the supplied names.
Choice between Mavalvala and Schnabel for the detector implementation is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Loss-DiVincenzo proposal and its experimental realisation produced electron-spin qubits in quantum dots, with coherent control, readout and now silicon devices compatible with semiconductor manufacturing. Qubit coherence and fidelity are exactly the issues central to making quantum devices useful.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo made the original theory proposal and Vandersypen led key experimental demonstrations of spin control; others (Kouwenhoven, Marcus, Yacoby, Tarucha) also made decisive experimental contributions, so the experimental credit is spread.
assessment.maturity: The platform is maturing rapidly with high-fidelity two-qubit gates, but scaling is still being demonstrated; recognition is somewhat early relative to superconducting circuits and ion traps.
uncertainties: Experimental credit is distributed among several leading groups.
Whether the field has opened a distinct new regime of physics or mainly an engineering platform is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states, with strong theoretical originality and clean experimental confirmation in HgTe wells.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theory proposals, and Molenkamp led the HgTe experimental demonstration following Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's prediction; the credit in the theory-to-experiment chain is contested, since Zhang's group contributions and the Kane-Mele graphene proposal differ in practical realisation.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced, with a stable interpretation across several materials; recognition is timely but partly overlaps in subject with the 2016 topological-phase prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and uncertain credit for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang.
This is outside my core expertise and I defer to condensed matter colleagues.
